title: Sephiria Secret Rooms — How to Find Hidden Rooms (Cracked Walls)
description: Find hidden rooms by checking cracked dungeon walls, opening them with an attack, and confirming the room on your map.
meta: Updated 26 October 2026. Practical route and caveats based on the Steam Basic Guide and player reports, plus a numbered wall check and a table of walls that will not open.
body:
Find Sephiria secret rooms by checking dungeon walls for a crack and striking it — that wall check is how the hidden room opens. Inside are supplies (leaves, Artifacts or Tablets, dice, or rare potions), and the finds count toward the Traveler achievement.

How to spot cracked walls

  • Scan dungeon walls for subtle cracks near the top — they are small, so sweep each corridor wall once.
  • Walk up and strike the crack. A notification confirms the find.
  • The room then appears on the map without a drawn passage.
  • The same guide’s Traveler note says the crack is not always along the bottom of the room. If the lower wall looks clean, check the upper edge before you leave.

The wall check, as a checklist

  1. Clear the floor first — the wall check only makes sense once the room is quiet.
  2. Walk the perimeter and compare each wall face and its upper border against the neighbouring tiles.
  3. Hit anything cracked or visually mismatched several times; the break can be a single line along the top edge.
  4. Read the notification, not the damage number. The guide names the notification as the confirmation that the wall opened.
  5. Check the map afterwards — an opened room may not draw a connecting line, so do not use the map as proof.
  6. Leave a wall alone once a full sweep shows no crack. No uncracked opening is documented.

When a wall is not openable

The guide documents one opening method: a crack, struck. Everything in the table follows from that, so a wall that fails every row is a wall to leave.

What you seeWhat it meansWhat to do
Bottom of the wall clean, nothing obvious aboveThe crack is not always along the bottomCheck the upper edge before walking away
No crack on any face after a full sweepNo documented opening exists for an uncracked wallStop searching that wall
Several hits, no notificationThe notification is the stated confirmationTreat the attempt as failed and move on
Room marked, corridor not drawnThe passage is never drawn on the mapGo back to the wall you already opened
Wall beside the table after ErmaA crackless passage reported by playersWalk under it instead of hunting a crack

What’s inside

The Steam Basic Guide’s node entry lists money boxes, artifact or slab rewards, dice, and rare potion boxes. Its secrets section also lists buffs, extra dice, leaves, bonus experience, or a choice of items. The guide gives no drop rates, so open the room and use whatever is actually inside.

Does the map show them?

Only after you open one. Cracked walls do not render on the map beforehand, which is why the “hidden room” phrasing fits: you find them by eye, not by minimap.

The post-Erma lore room

After defeating Erma, cross the bridge; on the left side of the table in the next room you can walk under the wall—no crack required. Players report it as mostly lore.

If you cannot find the entrance

  • The minimap shows nothing: look at the room walls first. The guide describes the map marker as a result of discovery, not a clue you can follow beforehand.
  • A crack is hard to see: check the upper edge of the wall, move close, and strike the suspected crack. Use the discovery notification to confirm success.
  • The room is marked but no corridor is drawn: return to the wall you opened; the guide explicitly notes that the passage does not appear on the map.
  • You are following the post-Erma tip: use the table-side passage described above. It is a different player-reported secret from the cracked-wall rooms.

Common mistakes

  • Sweeping only the bottom of each wall. The guide’s own note says the crack can sit higher, so a clean lower wall proves nothing.
  • Using the minimap to search. Nothing is drawn until the room is open, so a blank map is not evidence that the floor has none.
  • Leaving after one pass. Cracks are small, and a second look down the same corridor is cheaper than a repeat run.
  • Hunting a crack at the post-Erma table. That one is walk-under and player-reported, not a cracked wall.
  • Reading the reward tables as a guaranteed payout. The record lists possible outcomes and publishes no rate for any of them.

What the community record lists

Rewards are not fixed per room. The community record lists four outcome types, and the safe way to read the table is “possible”, not “guaranteed”:

RewardWhat the record saysHow to treat it
DiceOne or two dice, used to reroll item rewardsPossible, not guaranteed
ConsumablesTwo random consumablesDo not assume every room gives two
Random artifactListed as significantly rarer than the other outcomesRare possibility; no published rate
Mystic PotCombines up to three deposited artifacts into one tabletWeigh the inventory cost before using

Consumables seen in these rooms

ItemEffect as recorded
Focus PotionRecover 20% MP
Apple JuiceHeal 1 HP per second for 30 seconds
Nebbiolo’s Stubbornness+4 Physical damage
Tempradillo’s Passion+4 Fire damage
Ugni Blanc’s Mist+4 Cold damage
Malbec’s Depth+4 Lightning damage

Source: community secret-room record (sephiria.net), checked 9 November 2026. These are observations from one version; the in-game tooltip wins if they disagree. No percentages are published for the artifact outcome, so none are printed here.

What is still unknown

Four questions come up every time these rooms are discussed, and none of them is settled by the sources behind this page:

QuestionStatusHow to handle it
How many rooms a floor holdsNot documented, and no per-floor placement is givenSweep the floor you are on instead of planning around an expected count
Whether rooms respawnNot documentedTreat each crack as a one-off find
The artifact outcome’s rateListed as rarer, with no percentageDo not farm a floor expecting one
Whether ranged or area damage counts as strikingThe sources describe walking up and strikingUse the melee hit the guide describes

Quick FAQ

Do I need a key or an item to open one?

No item is mentioned for these rooms. The documented action is striking the crack itself, so nothing has to be bought or carried first.

Why did the room appear with no corridor?

Because the passage is not drawn. The room gets marked after discovery while the connecting line does not appear, so the wall you broke stays the landmark.

Does hitting an uncracked wall ever work?

Nothing in the sources describes an uncracked wall opening. The one exception on this page is the post-Erma table passage, and that one is walked under rather than struck.

Are the rewards worth the detour?

Sometimes. The record lists dice, consumables, a rarer artifact and the Mystic Pot with no rates, so the detour pays when the floor is already clear.

How many secret rooms are there?

The “Traveler” achievement records finding one. The Steam guide does not establish a fixed total number of rooms.

Do they respawn?

The Steam guide does not document respawn behavior; treat each crack as a dungeon find, not a repeatable room.

The Steam Basic Guide identifies its main content as version 0.7.31 with some updates through 0.7.35. Its cracked-wall instructions are clear, but current room placement and reward pools may differ. Treat the crackless post-Erma room as a separate community report.
